title: Romeo and Juliet, Fantasy-Overture
hook: Shakespeare’s play in twenty minutes, told through a feud, a love song and a funeral march.

painting.title: Romeo and Juliet
painting.pairingNote: The lovers’ parting at dawn on Juliet’s balcony, painted in the same two years that Tchaikovsky wrote the first version of the overture.

facts: In 1869 Mily Balakirev, the leader of the group of Russian composers in St Petersburg, suggested *Romeo and Juliet* to the 29-year-old Tchaikovsky. He sent detailed advice on the plan and even on the keys, and Tchaikovsky dedicated the work to him.

The first version was played in Moscow on 16 March 1870, conducted by Nikolai Rubinstein, and made little impression. Tchaikovsky revised it twice. The version played today dates from 1880 and was first heard in Tbilisi in 1886.

It does not tell the play scene by scene. It picks three ideas: a solemn hymn for Friar Laurence, a violent theme for the feud between the two families, and a love theme for Romeo and Juliet, and sets them against each other in [[sonata-form|sonata form]].
The love theme became one of the most famous melodies Tchaikovsky wrote, and film and television have borrowed it ever since.
bigPicture.inOneLine: the friar’s hymn, the street fight, the love song, the fight again, and a funeral march for the lovers.

movements.heading: Romeo and Juliet
movements.tempo: Andante non tanto quasi moderato – Allegro giusto – Moderato assai
movements.summary: A slow introduction, then a fast and stormy main section, then a slow epilogue. The fast section is in [[sonata-form|sonata form]]: the feud is the first theme, the love song the second, and when both come back the feud wins. In the epilogue the love theme returns one last time, broken, over a funeral drumbeat.

mainIdeas.name: Friar Laurence
mainIdeas.description: a slow, hymn-like [[chorale|chorale]], first in clarinets and bassoons.

mainIdeas.name: The feud
mainIdeas.description: a fast, angry theme in B minor, with short stabbing chords and crashing cymbals like clashing swords.

mainIdeas.name: The love theme
mainIdeas.description: a long, rising melody in D-flat major, first on English horn and violas together.

mainIdeas.name: The bedroom music
mainIdeas.description: soft, rocking chords in [[muted|muted]] strings, like a sigh.

stops.hear: Clarinets and bassoons play a slow, solemn hymn, low and quiet
stops.happening: The introduction. The hymn stands for Friar Laurence

stops.hear: The strings answer with dark, anxious sighs; then the harp plucks soft chords under the woodwind
stops.happening: The introduction grows. A sense of fate hangs over it

stops.hear: The music tightens and grows louder; a drum roll, then a hush
Fast, angry music in the strings, with short stabbing chords
stops.happening: The [[exposition|exposition]] begins: the feud theme, in B minor

stops.hear: Cymbals crash on the off-beats while the strings rush up and down
stops.happening: The street fight between Montagues and Capulets

stops.hear: Everything calms down. English horn and violas sing a long, rising melody
stops.happening: The love theme, in D-flat major

stops.hear: Soft, rocking chords in the muted strings, like breathing
stops.happening: The lovers alone. A gentle interlude inside the love music

stops.hear: The love theme returns high in flutes and oboes, a horn weaving a line beneath it; it swells and then settles
stops.happening: The love theme at full length. The end of the exposition

stops.hear: The feud theme breaks in again; trumpets and horns blare out the friar’s hymn against it
stops.happening: The [[development|development]]. The feud and the friar collide

stops.hear: The angry feud theme returns, shorter than before
The love theme in the full orchestra, at full strength, now in D major
The fight music cuts into the love theme; loud, crashing chords break it off
The timpani beat a slow, steady pulse; a low note is held underneath
stops.happening: The epilogue, a funeral march, now in B major

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: The woodwinds play a soft hymn; the strings recall the love theme, rising high; then loud final chords
stops.happening: A last farewell. The overture ends in B major

notice: The friar’s hymn returns in the middle of the fight, loud in the brass. Listen for slow notes cutting through fast ones.
The love theme appears three times: tender in the exposition, at full strength in the recapitulation, and broken in the epilogue. Compare how it sounds each time.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Semyon Bychkov recorded the overture with the Czech Philharmonic in Prague, on the first album of his “Tchaikovsky Project”, a cycle of the symphonies, the piano concertos and other orchestral works. On the Spotify album it is track 5, after the *Pathétique* Symphony.

threads.title: Three ideas, one story
threads.body: Tchaikovsky reduced the play to three forces: the friar, the feud and the love. The drama is in how they meet.

threads.title: Minor to major, but not a happy ending
threads.body: The overture begins in B minor and ends in B major. The major here sounds like peace after death, not victory.

threads.title: Ten years of revision
threads.body: The overture took three versions and more than a decade to reach its final form. The love theme survived every revision.

threads.title: Tchaikovsky and Shakespeare
threads.body: He returned to Shakespeare later, in *The Tempest* (1873) and *Hamlet* (1888).
